title: Inspections tab with not-started, all N/A, deleted, moved and many inspections
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with 'Customers - View' and 'Work orders - View'.
  2. An asset with: a not-started inspection; an all-N/A completed inspection; an inspection whose run-on work order is deleted; an inspection whose lines went onto a different work order then deleted.
  3. An asset moved between customers; an archived/deleted template; two inspections sharing a completion time; and an asset with about 150 inspections (seed in bulk).
custom_steps:
1. Confirm a not-started inspection shows dashes for completion date, technician and findings, and offers no action.
2. Confirm an all-N/A completed inspection reads as no issues and never needs action.
3. Delete the run-on work order and confirm the inspection stays listed with a dash in the work order column and remains usable; delete a different work order the lines were built onto and confirm the row returns to Needs action.
4. Move the asset to another customer (all inspections still listed); archive/delete the template (name+version shown as they were, never 'unknown'); confirm tied completion times keep a stable order; and confirm ~150 rows show without paging.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • For a not-started inspection, the completion date, technician and findings show dashes and no action is offered.
  • A completed inspection whose responses are all N/A reads as having no issues and never needs action.
  • If the run-on work order has been deleted, the inspection stays listed, the work order column shows a dash rather than a broken link, and the row stays usable.
  • If the asset has been moved to a different customer, all of its inspections are still listed.
  • If the template has been archived or deleted, the row shows the template name and version as they were at the time, never "unknown".
  • If two inspections share a completion time, their order is stable rather than varying between loads.
  • If the work order the lines were built onto is deleted and it is not the run-on work order, the row returns to Needs action rather than a Done state that points nowhere.
  • An asset with about 150 inspections shows them without paging; above roughly 200 rows a date filter or paging is needed (follow-up work).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9103 (S5 — Inspection history on the asset record); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S5; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-E1: “For a not-started inspection, the completion date, technician and findings show dashes and no action is offered”
  • S5-E2: “A completed inspection whose responses are all N/A reads as having no issues and never needs action”
  • S5-E3: “If the work order the inspection was run on has been deleted, the inspection remains listed, the work order column shows a dash rather than a broken link, and the row remains usable. This requires an inspection to outlive its work order rather than being removed with it”
  • S5-E4: “If the asset has been moved to a different customer, all of its inspections are still listed. The tab is the asset's history”
  • S5-E5: “If the template has been archived or deleted, the row shows the template name and version as they were at the time, never "unknown"”
  • S5-E6: “If two inspections share a completion time, the order between them is stable rather than varying between loads”
  • S5-E7: “If the work order the lines were built onto is deleted and it is not the work order the inspection was run on, the row returns to Needs action rather than showing a Done state that points nowhere”
  • S5-E8: “An asset inspected weekly for three years has roughly 150 rows, which the list shows without paging. Above roughly 200 rows the list will need a date filter or paging, which is follow-up work”

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.
